evidence.title: Violet Bathurst, Lady Apsley
evidence.text: Violet Emily Mildred Bathurst, Lady Apsley, CBE( née Meeking; 29 April 1895 – 19 January 1966) was a British Conservative Party politician.

evidence.title: Violet Bathurst, Lady Apsley
evidence.text: Upon the death of her husband, Lord Apsley, she succeeded him as Member of Parliament( MP) for Bristol Central in a 1943 by-election.

evidence.title: Violet Bathurst, Lady Apsley
evidence.text: She held the seat until 1945 when it was taken by Labour.

evidence.title: Violet Bathurst, Lady Apsley
evidence.text: Violet Mildred Emily Meeking was born on 29 April 1895 in Marylebone, London.

evidence.title: Violet Bathurst, Lady Apsley
evidence.text: She was the daughter of Captain Bertram Meeking of the 10th Hussars and his wife, Violet Charlotte( née Fletcher).

evidence.title: Violet Bathurst, Lady Apsley
evidence.text: She would later use the name" Viola".

evidence.title: Violet Bathurst, Lady Apsley
evidence.text: On 27 February 1924, she married Lord Apsley and they had two sons: Henry Allen John( 1927–2011) and George Bertram( 1929–2010).

evidence.title: Violet Bathurst, Lady Apsley
evidence.text: Apsley gained her pilot's licence in 1930 and served in the Auxiliary Territorial Service during the Second World War, resigning her commission after being elected to Parliament.

evidence.title: Violet Bathurst, Lady Apsley
evidence.text: Her husband died in an aircraft accident in 1942, and she succeeded him as Member of Parliament( MP) for Bristol Central, winning a 1943 by-election with a majority of 1,559.

evidence.title: Violet Bathurst, Lady Apsley
evidence.text: In the 1945 general election Lady Apsley lost her seat.

evidence.title: Violet Bathurst, Lady Apsley
evidence.text: She contested the Bristol North East seat between 1947 and 1951 but was not re-elected to Parliament.

evidence.title: Violet Bathurst, Lady Apsley
evidence.text: Between 1952 and 1954 she was a member of the Central Council of the Victoria League.

evidence.title: Violet Bathurst, Lady Apsley
evidence.text: She held numerous offices in the Conservative Party, and was National Chairman of the Women's Section of the British Legion.

evidence.title: Violet Bathurst, Lady Apsley
evidence.text: She was made a Commander of the Order of the British Empire( CBE) in the 1952 Queen's Birthday Honours," for public and social services".
